section_map.title: Purpose
section_map.body:
This document defines the governance principles applicable to the **Document Identity** component.

Its purpose is to establish the architectural rules that preserve the integrity, stability, uniqueness, and permanence of document identities throughout the Documentation Framework.

This document defines **how document identities shall be governed** from an architectural perspective.

It does **not** define organisational workflows, approval processes, repository policies, or operational governance, which are the responsibility of the **Governance Layer**.

---

section_map.title: Introduction
section_map.body:
Document Identity is a foundational architectural concept upon which every other Documentation Framework component depends.

Consequently, its governance differs from the governance of ordinary document attributes.

Once assigned, a document identity becomes a permanent architectural asset whose integrity shall be preserved throughout the complete lifetime of the document.

The governance of document identities therefore focuses on preserving architectural correctness rather than managing document evolution.

---

section_map.title: Governance Objectives
Governance Principles
Permanence
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall remain permanently associated with the document for which it was assigned.

---

section_map.title: Immutability
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall never be modified after assignment.

Any modification to document content, metadata, classification, governance state, or storage location shall preserve the same identity.

---

section_map.title: Uniqueness
section_map.body:
Every document shall possess one and only one canonical identity.

Duplicate identities are prohibited.

---

section_map.title: Non-Reusability
section_map.body:
Once retired, a Document Identity shall never be assigned to another document.

---

section_map.title: Traceability
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall remain suitable for long-term architectural reference.

Historical references shall remain valid regardless of document evolution.

---

section_map.title: Independence
Governance Responsibilities
Governance Rules
section_map.body: The following architectural rules shall always apply.

section_map.title: Rule 1
section_map.body:
Every document shall possess exactly one Document Identity.

---

section_map.title: Rule 2
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall never be modified.

---

section_map.title: Rule 3
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall never be duplicated.

---

section_map.title: Rule 4
section_map.body:
A Document Identity shall never be reassigned.

---

section_map.title: Rule 5
section_map.body:
A retired Document Identity shall remain permanently reserved.

---

section_map.title: Rule 6
section_map.body:
Every architectural reference shall target a valid Document Identity.

---

section_map.title: Rule 7
section_map.body:
No component other than Document Identity shall define identity semantics.

---

section_map.title: Governance Ownership
section_map.body:
The ownership of document identity is exclusively assigned to the Document Identity component.

```text

                    Document Identity
                    │
                    ├── Defines identity
                    ├── Owns identity semantics
                    ├── Governs identity integrity
                    ├── Preserves identity stability
                    └── Defines validation rules

```

Other Documentation Framework components consume document identities but never own them.

---

section_map.title: Governance Interactions
Metadata
section_map.body:
Metadata associates descriptive information with a Document Identity.

Metadata governance shall never alter document identity.

---

section_map.title: Classification
section_map.body:
Classification governs document categorisation.

Classification governance shall preserve document identity.

---

section_map.title: Governance Layer
section_map.body:
The Governance Layer manages document processes.

Document Identity governance manages the architectural integrity of identities.

These responsibilities are complementary.

---

section_map.title: Registry
section_map.body:
Registry governs document registration.

Registry shall preserve the canonical identity defined by this component.

---

section_map.title: Relationships
section_map.body:
Relationships govern semantic associations between identified documents.

Relationship governance shall preserve identity integrity.

---

section_map.title: Knowledge Graph
section_map.body:
Knowledge Graph governs graph representations.

The graph shall preserve canonical document identities.

---

section_map.title: Governance Compliance
Governance Violations
Relationship with Validation
section_map.body:
Governance defines the architectural rules.

Validation verifies compliance with those rules.

```text

               Governance
                    │
                    ▼

           Architectural Rules
                    │
                    ▼

               Validation
                    │
                    ▼

          Compliance Verification

```

The two specifications are complementary.

---

section_map.title: Relationship with Lifecycle
section_map.body:
Lifecycle describes how a Document Identity exists over time.

Governance defines the rules that shall be respected throughout that lifecycle.

Lifecycle answers:

> *When does an identity exist?*

Governance answers:

> *How shall that identity be preserved?*

---

section_map.title: Summary
section_map.body:
The Document Identity Governance specification defines the architectural principles that preserve the integrity, permanence, uniqueness, and stability of document identities throughout the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the governance responsibilities owned exclusively by the Document Identity component while clearly separating them from operational governance responsibilities defined by the Governance Layer.

These governance principles ensure that every Document Identity remains a permanent, immutable, and canonical architectural reference, providing a stable foundation for all other Documentation Framework components.

---

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 5. Out of Scope

The following roles are separate from document identity semantic ownership. Area labels, registered capability contracts and operational executors are identified separately; naming an owner proves no implemented service.

| Received responsibility | Responsible contract/role | Operational or semantic boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document metadata | Metadata plus applicable semantic domain owners | Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile; descriptive representation does not replace identity |
| Document classification | Classification | Family/Type and other category meanings remain mutable and separately owned |
| Registry management | Registry | Catalog/lookup contracts and provenance; actual registration/lookup executed by an applicable system/process |
| Discovery services | Discovery area: Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph, Navigation, Search | Area groups capabilities; it is not another component or mandatory routing intermediary |
| Workflow management | Workflow and applicable Policies | Subject-specific transitions/rules; DMS/tool/manual operation, not an implemented DF workflow engine |
| Version control | Documentary edition contracts versus source-control systems/adapters | Version/Revision/Status semantics follow applicable governance/edition contracts; repository commits and Source Control Integration adapters do not define them |
| Repository management | DMS or other applicable external system | Organization, storage, permissions and physical-location execution |
| Storage technologies | Applicable implementations/external systems | Persistence mechanisms preserve applicable representation/provenance requirements |
| Identifier generation algorithms | Applicable allocation executor | Generate/allocate under identity-domain rules and collision/reservation evidence; no algorithm supplied here |
| Persistence mechanisms | Applicable implementation/external system | Store identity/edition/context records without acquiring identity semantics |

Governance is an area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines; it is not a single invented component owning all operational management. Reviews records examined scope/results; Baselines defines immutable selected exact approved editions and context. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or snapshot inclusion.

---

# 7. Core Architectural Characteristics

Within its declared allocation/preservation contract, an assigned logical identity shall be unique for the document in its domain, stable through normal evolution, and never reassigned to a different document. Domain qualification is required to interpret uniqueness; an identifier string alone is not universally unique across unregistered domains.

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key under its applicable contract, not every mutable record about that identity. Identity-state evidence, references, location, descriptors and exact-edition coordinates can evolve under their own owner rules without automatically replacing the key. References and aliases interpret an existing logical document; they do not license another document to reuse its identity. Allocated and retired identities remain reserved.

Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition changes. If a necessary authorized schema/ID migration would change an otherwise immutable representation/allocation contract, first assess and explicitly reconcile the governing previous/new rules with responsible identity/domain sources. Record old→new mappings, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, historical/reference/context effects, exact source editions, affected consumers and transition verification before coordinated application. Preserve original representations and historical immutable snapshot selections; never retarget old members or reassign retired allocations to another document. No blanket permission for arbitrary identity changes or two contradictory governing rules for one operation is introduced. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

Long-term understandable/referenceable identity is a requirement and design objective supported by qualified domain/canonicalization and actual preservation/resolution evidence. It guarantees neither universally understood bare strings nor future content availability. Exact-edition references additionally identify the intended Version/Revision and relevant bytes/context; logical identity alone selects neither an exact edition nor Baseline membership.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define documentary transition, decision, review and snapshot requirements; actual operation remains with DMS/tool/manual processes and CMS change scope. Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct. A state list alone is neither a universal permission graph nor an implemented workflow.

Baselines selects an explicitly identified immutable set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Identity alone cannot select an exact member; eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion remain separate checks. Draft successors neither inherit membership nor retarget older snapshots. Retired identities preserve reservations/history without implying current document publication or resolver availability.

## 3.1 Document

A **Document** is a logical documentary knowledge entity under an applicable recognition and normalization scope. An exact document edition records particular content/descriptors and context; a file or representation is not the logical entity itself.

Normalized identity obligations apply after the functional-file exclusion in §2. Template definitions/instances, Metadata Elements and graph/relationship records can have other qualified entity contracts; not every knowledge asset or endpoint receives a DF document ID.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify the actual subject, scope and exact edition/representation examined. Distinguish valid logical identity from coordinates, Status, maturity and membership; registration or recognition alone proves neither approval nor complete conformance.

---

## 3.2 Document Identity

A **Document Identity** identifies the same logical document under a declared **Domain+Identifier** allocation/preservation contract. Uniqueness applies within that domain, not to every bare string in every external system. Identity remains associated with the document through ordinary changes and is not reconstructed from current classification, path or edition.

The assigned key, canonical identifier representation, mutable identity-record state and exact edition are separate. DID-001 establishes the applicable architecture; full peer schema integration remains pending.

**Evidence boundary:** Check domain qualification, actual allocation/reservation records, intended document continuity and examined source editions. No successful allocation, universal resolver or arbitrary key change is implied by the definition.

---

## 3.7 Identity Stability

**Identity Stability** requires valid assigned identity to remain associated with the same document through ordinary content/descriptor, classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition evolution. The key is stable under its governing allocation contract; mutable state/location/reference records do not automatically replace it.

Necessary authorized schema/ID migration that changes an otherwise immutable representation/allocation rule first explicitly reconciles governing previous/new contracts with responsible identity/domain owners. Record old→new mapping, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, history/reference/context, exact editions, affected consumers and transition checks before coordinated application. Preserve historical immutable snapshot selections; no arbitrary reassignment or simultaneous contradictory governing rules is introduced.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual target continuity, representations and owner/consumer evidence. Stability supports preserved reference interpretation but does not ensure a running resolver or retrieved content. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

---

# 5. Relationship with Metadata

Document Identity owns identity/domain/allocation meanings. Metadata defines/represents descriptors under their responsible semantic owners; representing an identity value does not redefine or replace identity. Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. The following preserves the five received contrast subjects with actual qualifications.

| Received identity-side contrast | Received Metadata-side contrast | Qualified interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Identifies a document | Describes a document | Key meaning versus descriptors; values may represent identity under its domain constraints |
| Permanent | Evolves over time | Same-document association/non-reuse versus actual descriptor/entity/edition lifecycle; not every value is mutable |
| Immutable | May change | Assigned key versus mutable support records/representations; identity values preserve owner constraints |
| Unique | May contain repeated values | Domain uniqueness versus actual per-element occurrence/uniqueness rules; some represented values have identity constraints |
| Stable | Version dependent | Logical identity versus actual descriptor/entity/edition context; not universal Metadata Version dependence |

Metadata Elements, definitions and represented instance values have their own qualified identity/lifecycle subjects. Semantic separation does not guarantee independent editions or content-free verification; coordinated descriptor/content changes may be needed. No Metadata Element ID, mandatory catalog field or Profile is created by this Concept source.

MTD-003 §8 says Schema defines Metadata Elements, while MTD-013 assigns canonical definitions/catalog responsibility to Dictionary. These actual owner-source claims and catalog/Profile gaps remain pending full reconciliation. This table follows adopted role boundaries without certifying a merged schema or complete peer propagation.

---

# 8. Concept Boundaries

**This document defines concepts only.** The **Document Identity component** also defines architectural, model, element/schema, allocation/preservation, lifecycle, validation, governance, reference and controlled-evolution contracts through their responsible sources. It does not itself execute identifier generation, storage, assignment or management services.

This source can explain logical domain/identifier/reference/representation requirements without supplying complete syntax/schema catalogs, algorithm code, physical persistence or operational permissions. Detailed constraints and implementation choices remain qualified by their owners. Explicit conceptual limits do not prohibit legitimate logical contract requirements or assign all responsibility solely to Specification.

Preserve compatible meaning where feasible. Necessary changes require previous/new rationale, exact affected editions, owners/consumers, dependencies, compatibility and transition checks. For working document editions, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Each changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation of unchanged source changes neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Other entity-domain numbering/lifecycle remains separate.

| Approved | Preserved | Formal approval needs its own exact-edition evidence; status/identity alone selects no Baseline member |
| Published | Preserved | Publication and assignment/preservation need separate actual observations; availability is not guaranteed by the identity label |
| Archived | Preserved | Archiving a document/representation does not by itself retire the logical identity; distinguish historical Active/Archived terminology from a governed identity-state assertion |
| Obsolete | Preserved | Obsolescence may preserve assigned-key history; any retirement requires a distinct responsible decision, not a guessed state mapping |
| Deleted | Retired | Received correlation is not a rule that every file/edition/index deletion retires logical identity; require explicit retirement scope/decision and preserved reservation/history |

The operational state does not automatically determine or reallocate the assigned key. Actual domain/process rules can require coordinated decisions and evidence; semantic separation does not mean all subjects are operationally unrelated. A declared status is not a universal permission graph. A newly edited Draft successor neither inherits Baseline inclusion nor retargets an immutable approved snapshot. The selected transition applicability in §7 still applies; a status row grants no missing edge.

---

# 9. Relationship with Other Components

The six original interaction headings are retained. Definition, required consumption, registration/connection ownership, projection and execution are distinct. Statements below are architectural requirements with evidence boundaries, not claims that every consuming system already implements them.

---

## 9.1. Metadata

Metadata can describe identity/lifecycle facts under their responsible semantic owners. Mutable descriptor records and state assertions do not automatically reallocate the key. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles and actual descriptor authority remain with applicable Metadata contracts; this document creates no new Metadata Element, canonical Profile or merged field catalog.

Actual required contracts are assessed in scope: the DID README declares identity consumption of Metadata descriptive concepts, while DID-009§§5/10 declares Metadata→Document Identity and no consuming-component dependency. Retain both source claims for owner/core-versus-descriptor/interface reconciliation under ARC-004; changing a name or projecting data cannot hide a genuine required cycle.

---

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns categories. Ordinary classification changes retain the assigned key and stable allocation series; current Family/Type/Component do not regenerate it. Actual category/reference/edition effects still require the applicable owner checks. Classification definitions and their entity keys/lifecycles are not automatically normalized document identities.

---

## 9.3. Governance

Governance is the area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines, not a single new component. These owners define applicable process, decision, review and exact-snapshot contracts. Actual DMS/tool/manual operation and CMS change records remain separate from DF semantic responsibility.

Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and Baseline membership are distinct. Preserve same-document assignment through ordinary governance evolution; perform actual retirement only with responsible scope/decision/evidence. An identity label or local validation grants neither formal approval nor snapshot inclusion.

---

## 9.4. Registry

Registry owns registration/index records with source/edition provenance and freshness/current/historical/snapshot context. Such records may change while identifying the same logical key. Registration alone proves no valid allocation or completed retirement propagation; actual executor observations and coverage are required. No universal Registry intermediary or implemented lookup/resolver is imposed.

---

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance. Document Identity supplies document endpoint meanings; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts. Incoming document-targeting population0..N does not require a reference merely for an identity to exist.

Actual target validity needs the intended existing qualified document or exact edition/context. Stable identity supports historical interpretation but does not guarantee every connection remains valid or retrievable. Record dangling, ambiguous, stale and unavailable references; never silently create or retarget an identity. Lifecycle changes to relation records follow their owners without automatically reallocating the document key.

---

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph may project an identity as a node whose logical document key remains stable under ordinary evolution. Node properties, state descriptions, edges, projections, source provenance, freshness and even physical node representation may change; this is not a requirement that every graph node's bytes remain unchanged.

Graph projections retain underlying identity/relationship authority and exact-edition context; they do not create competing keys or prove complete propagation. Required consumer→provider uses, scope/source interfaces and cycle constraints follow ARC-004/005. No Registry→Graph→Baseline operational chain or complete globally acyclic graph is established.

---

# 10. Architectural Constraints

The six original constraint responsibilities are retained with actual subject and evidence boundaries.

| Received constraint responsibility | Qualified requirement / evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Assignment only once | One governed association of an assigned key with its intended logical document; repeated observations/registrations do not allocate another key; actual assignment/history evidence required |
| Identity never changes | Ordinary evolution preserves the qualified key/same-document association; mutable support records and necessary contract migration assessment in §3.2 are distinct |
| Identity never duplicated | Domain-scoped qualified uniqueness assessed through actual allocation/collision/reservation coverage; bare strings, copies and graph projections are not automatically new allocations |
| Identity never reused | Allocated and retired keys remain reserved against assignment to another document; preserve original/history evidence |
| Retirement does not invalidate historical references | Preserve intended historical target interpretation/reservations/context; actual connection validity and current/future retrieval need separate observations |
| Implementation technology independence | Domain semantics are not redefined by storage/adapters; actual implementations still satisfy applicable logical representation/interface/evidence requirements |

A requirement is not evidence of successful enforcement. Record rules/source edition, subject/artifacts, executor, coverage, observations and unresolved conditions. No current global uniqueness, live resolver or guaranteed future state is asserted by these rows.

# 1. Purpose

This document defines identity-validation requirements, their evidence boundaries and result interpretation for **applicable assigned normalized logical documents** under declared identity-domain contracts. It specifies what is evaluated without choosing an implementation, allocator, resolver or runtime validation engine.

Identify the actual subject, governing domain/rules and source editions, exact artifacts/bytes and relevant context before claiming a result. Distinguish the assigned Domain+Identifier key, its same-document association, mutable lifecycle/reference/descriptor/projection records, physical representations and exact document editions. Unassigned is a pre-allocation documentary subject, not an existing assigned key.

Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md is non-normalized at every location. Such files require no normalized identity/header solely because they are files; applicable content, references, history and hash checks remain. Other entity kinds and external domains need their own responsible contracts.

Requirements and local observations do not by themselves establish implemented conformance, actual allocation, formal approval, publication, Baseline membership or global architectural integrity. DF owns documentary semantics; actual DMS/tool/manual execution and CMS change governance retain their separate scopes.

---

# 2. Introduction

Validation evaluates identified requirements against identified artifacts and records actual checks, observations, coverage, executor and limits. It does not ensure that every identity in every context is already correct or remains correct forever. Preserve the five received objective subjects: uniqueness, completeness, structural validity, internal consistency and architectural compliance; each claimed result is bounded by the applicable evaluated contract.

Identity-domain result scope is distinct from evidence access. A check may inspect relevant document content/headers, Metadata values, representations, allocation/retirement decisions, connection records, indexes or exact-edition context without claiming complete validation of document content, Metadata, governance, repositories or implementation behaviour. Do not infer that evidence in those domains is irrelevant merely because their rule ownership is separate.

Before evaluation, record the intended claim, actual subject/domain, exact inputs and relevant snapshots, applicable rules/editions, mandatory-check inventory, known owner conflicts, executor/method and external-observation context where relevant. After evaluation, record each performed check, observed result, omissions, missing evidence, limitations and output provenance. Those are evidence roles, not newly allocated Metadata Elements or a prescribed schema/API.

A selected subset of successful checks supports only those observations; it cannot be promoted to a full Valid identity claim while applicable mandatory checks, evidence or governing authority remain unresolved. §8 defines result meanings and aggregation.

---

# 4. Validation Scope

The five original scope labels remain, with their subject/property role clarified. Mandatory means evaluation is required when that responsibility applies to the declared identity claim, not that every label is a stored field or that absence of evidence implies success.

| Element / retained scope label | Validation | Actual subject/property and evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Domain | Mandatory when applicable | Governing qualification/rules/owner and actual population/reservation coverage |
| Identifier | Mandatory for applicable assigned key | Canonical representation, assignment interpretation and qualified uniqueness, not a bare syntax-only claim |
| Identity Integrity | Mandatory when applicable | Property assessed through assignment/preservation/retirement history; mutable support records distinguished |
| Identity Uniqueness | Mandatory when applicable | Property over the declared domain/population/history, with collision/reservation limits |
| Identity Consistency | Mandatory when applicable | Property of exact records/rules/context, with source authority and observations stated |

The received exclusions remain result/semantic-ownership boundaries: no complete Metadata, document, governance, repository or implementation validation is claimed by an identity-only check. Relevant values, content, representation and decision records may still be necessary identity evidence. Declare actual evidence inspected and the narrower conclusions drawn; do not silently extend a source-local result to a whole excluded domain.

Mandatory/prohibited field, lifecycle-state and Canonical Reference applicability depends on exact responsible contracts. Unresolved owner requirements remain visible under §3.1; narrower checks cannot certify an integrated complete record. Rule coverage also includes reference validation in §5.5; absence of a reference row in this received five-row scope table does not exempt an applicable reference requirement.

---

## 5.5. Reference Validation

For a document-targeting reference, check the intended existing qualified logical document or exact edition under its relation contract. Exact-edition targeting additionally pins coordinates/bytes and relevant context. Other endpoint kinds follow their own responsible identity contracts rather than automatically resolving to a DF document ID.

Incoming document-targeting population0..N permits an identity to have no incoming references; per-reference validity is a different question. Canonical/alias interpretation and logical target validity differ from present/future live retrieval. Record actual dangling, ambiguous, stale or unavailable observations with target, method, time/snapshot context, coverage and limits. Unperformed reference checks are not automatically successful or observed Unresolvable outcomes.

Document Identity owns document endpoint meaning; Relationships owns typed connection semantics/records and provenance, Registry registration/index records, and Knowledge Graph projections retain source authority. A consuming component may execute checks under those responsible contracts; it does not acquire every reference's semantics. Never create or silently retarget an identity to make a check pass.

---

# 8. Validation Outcomes

The four original outcome labels are retained with owner-defined semantic meanings. They are evaluation observations/results, not document Status, identity lifecycle, Milestone state, approval or Baseline membership. Executors may choose a representation/report format, not redefine these meanings silently.

| Outcome | Qualified meaning | Required evidence and scope |
|---|---|---|
| Valid | All applicable mandatory requirements for the declared identity claim were actually evaluated and satisfied in the identified scope, with no contrary observations or unresolved mandatory evidence/authority | Exact applicable rule inventory, inputs/context, completed checks and observations; no claim beyond coverage |
| Invalid | An actual observed violation of an applicable mandatory rule for the subject/context | Identify exact responsible rule/edition, actual artifact and violation; missing evidence alone is not proof of violation |
| Inconsistent | Actual conflicting identity-related information for the same intended subject/context | Record conflicting values/records and source context; legitimate edition/snapshot differences are not automatically conflict |
| Unresolvable | An actual performed check cannot establish the required intended target interpretation/resolution under the applicable reference contract/context | Record target, rules, performed method/observation and coverage; no blanket historical invalidity or perpetual availability inference |

**Coverage and aggregation contract:**

- Declare the identity claim and its applicable mandatory rules before deciding Valid. An arbitrary successful subset is only successful check evidence, not a full Valid identity claim; inapplicability needs responsible justification, not omission to manufacture success.
- Record applicability, performed/unperformed checks, missing evidence, unresolved owner authority and external observation limits separately from outcome labels. No fifth lifecycle/document state is created by these coverage facts. If required evidence, checks or authority remain unresolved, the broader Valid claim is withheld; do not default to Invalid or Unresolvable without an actual supporting observation.
- Negative observations may coexist: preserve all supported Invalid, Inconsistent and Unresolvable findings with their exact rules/subjects/context. Do not suppress a specific observation through a silent precedence rule. An overlapping mandatory violation is additionally Invalid only when its applicable rule and violation are established.
- Valid cannot coexist with contrary observations for the same aggregate claim/context. Per-check success may coexist with failures elsewhere, but the combined identity claim is not Valid. Any implementation that also needs one summary field must preserve the full observation set and disclose its explicit summary mapping without changing these meanings or manufacturing completeness.
- Contradictory governing contracts are recorded as authority/applicability limitations; they do not alone prove that the assessed subject violated a rule. Evaluate unambiguous subsets with explicit limits, and obtain responsible owner reconciliation before broader conformance claims.
- A later input/rule/context change requires assessment of the resulting artifacts. Earlier Valid, local PASS or stable logical identity does not automatically validate changed bytes, publish/approve them or select a Baseline.

This result contract is independent of how a checker is implemented. It supplies no operational checker, allocation, resolver, universal future guarantee or whole-framework certification.

---

# 9. Relationship with Other Components

The six original interaction headings are retained. Rule ownership, evidence access, actual execution, review and approval are separate. Registered capability names and area labels do not prove an installed executor or successful check.

---

## 9.1. Metadata

Metadata owns applicable descriptive definitions/schema/profile/instance rules under their semantic owners. Identity evaluation may inspect relevant identity/state/edition descriptors as evidence without claiming complete Metadata validation or redefining their domain meaning. A missing canonical descriptor definition/Profile remains visible; this document creates none.

The actual DID README declares identity consumption of Metadata descriptive concepts while DID-009§§5/10 declares Metadata→Document Identity/no consuming-component dependency. Both required-contract claims remain pending owner/core-versus-descriptor/interface reconciliation under ARC-004. An association/projection label does not remove a genuine required cycle.

---

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category validation. Identity checks may inspect changing Family/Type/Component values to verify that the stable allocated key was not improperly regenerated, without validating the entire category model. Other classification entity keys are not automatically DF document IDs; original source identity remains distinct from mutable categories.

---

## 9.3. Registry

Registry may execute or consume identity checks under the responsible identity/rule contracts while retaining registration/index ownership. Record exact source/edition/context and freshness; an index entry alone proves neither unique assignment nor completed validation. Registry cannot silently redefine result semantics or turn a partial catalog scan into global uniqueness/availability.

---

## 9.4. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records/provenance; Document Identity owns document endpoint meaning and the applicable identity checks. A consuming executor may check targets under those contracts without acquiring every relation's semantics. Other endpoints and exact editions retain their own context requirements. Graph projections and registration are not competing reference authorities or universal routing requirements.

---

## 9.5. Governance

Governance is the area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines, not a new component. Applicable owners can require identity checks and define documentary decision/evidence conditions without redefining identity semantics. Reviews records examined scope/findings; Baselines needs actual exact approved-edition selection, not merely an identity-check result.

Validation, formal approval, publication, exact edition Status and snapshot membership remain distinct events. DMS/tool/manual processes execute actual operations and CMS governs changes in its scope. A local validation outcome grants none of those other decisions automatically.

---

## 9.6. Automation

Automation is the area grouping applicable capabilities; Validation and Consistency Verification are actual registered checking components. Their implementations consume responsible domain contracts and record exact inputs/rules/checks/observations/coverage/executor/limits. Reviews can use those results without redefining identity meanings or turning technical PASS into approval.

This source supplies identity-validation rules, not code or a deployed engine. Actual automated, tool-assisted or manual execution identifies its responsible method/context and evidence. Definition ownership does not make the DF component itself the storage/permission/assignment service or certify complete implementation conformance.

---

# 10. Architectural Constraints

The six original constraint responsibilities remain with explicit subjects and conditions.

| Received constraint responsibility | Qualified requirement / evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Preserve identity immutability | Assess stable assigned key/association under the governing contract; mutable support records are separately interpreted |
| Never modify identities | Checking does not mutate the assessed key or silently repair input evidence; result/evidence output is a separate record |
| Never generate identities | No allocation, key creation or silent target substitution to satisfy a check; remediation is a separately governed action |
| Deterministic | For equivalent pinned inputs, rules and relevant observation context, apply stable owner meanings; disclose live/nondeterministic dependencies and actual context instead of context-free promises |
| Repeatable | Retain sufficient exact artifact/rule/context/method provenance to reproduce or explain the observations within stated limits; changed inputs/rules/context require new assessment |
| Implementation independent | Owner semantics do not choose a runtime; actual executors still meet applicable representation/interface/evidence obligations |

A result report may be written without modifying the assessed identity. Corrections to a working document or generated records need their own authorized change/version/provenance and later validation; validation itself is not permission for mutation. Record original evidence and actual failures rather than retrospectively converting them into success. No long-term/global outcome guarantee follows from these requirements.

---

```text
              Metadata Model
                    ↓

                 Level 3
             Metadata Schema
                    ↓

                 Level 4
            Metadata Profiles
                    ↓

                 Level 5
            Metadata Instances

```

Each level refines the previous one without altering its semantics.

---

# 7. Conceptual Entities

The Metadata Model is composed of the following conceptual entities.

## 7.1 Metadata

Represents the complete descriptive information associated with a document.

Metadata is composed of Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.2 Metadata Element

Represents one descriptive property of Metadata.

Each Metadata Element has one semantic meaning.

Metadata Elements are defined independently.

---

## 7.3 Metadata Value

Represents the value assigned to a Metadata Element for a specific document.

Values instantiate Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.4 Metadata Schema

Represents the formal organization of Metadata Elements.

The Schema determines which Metadata Elements may appear within a Metadata instance.

---

## 7.5 Metadata Profile

Represents a specialization of a Metadata Schema for a particular category of documents.

Profiles constrain, but do not redefine, the underlying Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.6 Metadata Instance

Represents the complete Metadata associated with one individual document.

Each Metadata Instance conforms to exactly one Metadata Profile.

---

# 8. Conceptual Relationships

The Metadata Model defines the following relationships.

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata | is composed of | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Element | possesses | Metadata Value |
| Metadata Schema | defines | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Instance | conforms to | Metadata Profile |
| Metadata Instance | contains | Metadata Values |

---

## 2. Normalized documents and functional files

Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md in this corpus is a non-normalized functional file. It retains its name and does not require Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline by virtue of document normalization. Do not infer a finding from absence of those fields. Do not automatically delete legitimate existing information.

These files remain in inventories, SHA-256 manifests, content reviews and applicable structural, terminology, reference and consistency checks. CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md retain their own entry/milestone IDs, states, dates and historical conventions. Their maintenance is not conditional on normalized document metadata.

The input corpus comprises 79 documents within normalization scope and 8 non-normalized files. Two normalized review documents are introduced by Step 3. Machine-readable exports attached to DF-RVW-002 are representations of its inventories and matrices, not independent normalized documents or new authorities. Each export identifies its parent document and edition in its manifest or accompanying report.

## 3. Classification contract

### 3.1. Uniform Type

Type identifies the primary responsibility of every normalized document and uses exactly one value from {Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference}. There are no special Type values for Foundation, Architecture, global roadmaps or review artifacts.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions. |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs. |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution. |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records. |

Use the spelling Behavior. Base, Core, Schema, Dictionary and Lifecycle are not additional Type values. A historical evolution account is Reference; a process or evolution plan is Behavior. Assess content and primary responsibility rather than filename or directory alone. Normative or informative authority is established by explicit statements/references, never by Type=Reference alone. Validation is not approval.

### 3.2. Family and Component

| Document category | Family | Component |
|---|---|---|
| Belongs to a component | Canonical component name | Same canonical name, when the field is used. |
| Foundation without a component | Foundation | Absent/not applicable. |
| Architecture without a component | Architecture | Absent/not applicable. |
| Global roadmap or global implementation strategy | Roadmap | Absent/not applicable. |
| This review's policy/report | Reviews | Reviews. |

Roadmap is an explicitly scoped documentary planning area for global, non-component plans. It reuses the received Family value in DF-RDM-001/002, not an invented component or Layer. These two documents use Type=Behavior. The existing Component=Documentation Framework in DF-RDM-002 must be assessed and removed from its working header in the scheduled UPDATE: the framework is the container, not a component of itself.

Component roadmaps belong to the component they plan and therefore use Family=component, Type=Behavior and matching Component, regardless of central storage under Roadmaps. Current component names are Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. DocumentIdentity is a directory alias, not a competing canonical component name.

Do not remove Component indiscriminately. The global roadmap decision is localized and does not remove it from component documents. Family/Type changes do not determine document identity or structural Layer allocation.

### 3.3. Class

Class remains a separate, optional semantic dimension. This policy does not create a complete Class vocabulary or make it mandatory. Retain received values as evidence, then assess each use in its document cycle. A value that merely repeats Type or misstates authority must be reconciled with evidence. New review artifacts omit Class because no additional distinction is needed. Optional does not mean unrestricted: any value used must have an explicit, non-conflicting definition.

## 4. Identity convention for this corpus and review artifacts

### 4.1. Representation and uniqueness

The identity domain is Documentation Framework. Its representation prefix is DF. A working normalized document identifier follows DF-SSS-NNN, where SSS is a registered three-letter uppercase allocation-series code and NNN is a three-digit positive allocation number, 001–999. The full identifier is unique within the domain. Numbers are allocated within a series; equal numeric suffixes across different series are not collisions.

Series codes are stable allocation namespaces, not the document's current Family, Type, component, location, version or revision. Preserve existing valid identifiers when those characteristics change. A series' original purpose is recorded for traceability, but it does not recalculate an existing document ID after reassignment/reclassification.

| Series | Received origin/purpose | Step 3 action |
|---|---|---|
| FND | Foundation documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| ARC | Framework Architecture documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| MTD | Metadata documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| DID | Document Identity documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| CLS | Classification documents | Preserve unambiguous allocations; resolve the nominal CLS-003 collision. |
| TPL | Templates documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| RDM | Planning documents | Preserve allocations even when Family becomes a component name. |
| RVW | Review policy and consolidated review report | Allocate 001 to this policy and 002 to DF-RVW-002 after collision checks. |

This is a corpus convention, not a format imposed on identities in other domains or an identifier-generation implementation. Scheduled reconciliation of DF-DID-005/010/014 owns its integration into the identity contract. Foundation and Classification must qualify the earlier Family/Type-based convention accordingly.

### 4.2. Allocation, reservations and retirement

New allocation requires an explicit series record and collision scan of headers, filenames, references, historical/reserved records and this review's allocation register. Do not reuse allocated/retired numbers. A gap does not prove availability; when allocation history is unavailable, record that limitation and use a documented allocation decision rather than infer a historical reservation. Missing IDs are not assigned to the eight functional files excluded in §2.

000 is not allocated under this working convention; it is not implicitly a README code. RVW-001/002 are the only new allocations at Step 3; no future numbers are reserved. At 999, do not widen the syntax or silently recycle: register another unused three-letter series with traceable continuation and preserve all old IDs. A new domain is a separate semantic decision, not a shortcut for renumbering this corpus.

Maintain an allocation register in DF-RVW-002's exports, including series, number, identifier, path, allocation status and evidence. Retired IDs remain reserved. The source archive and the input manifest preserve received declarations, including invalid ones; preservation is evidence, not acceptance of a collision.

### 4.3. Localized correction and historical syntax

No general ID migration is required by the adopted classification change. The nominal DF-CLS-003-ClassificationModel.md wrongly declares DF-CLS-001 and repeats the Architecture prose. Its correction is pending a distinct document recovery/update and path-scoped map. It is not a global DF-CLS-001→DF-CLS-003 replacement or an alias that makes one identifier resolve to two documents.

Operational references must resolve to the intended final identity/path after a coordinated correction. Historical examples such as META-DCL-001, or earlier roadmap forms containing RDM as an extra segment, must be explicitly qualified where historical or revised where they purport to prescribe the current working convention. Do not rewrite history as if the new convention had always existed.

Metadata Element IDs, document IDs, finding IDs, CHANGELOG numbers and Milestone IDs are separate entities. Creating this policy does not assign Metadata Element IDs or create element lifecycle/publication records.

## 5. Version, Revision, Status and Baseline

### 5.1. Received evidence

The 79 in-scope input documents declare Version 1.0 and Baseline 1.0; 73 declare Revision 0 and six Foundation documents do not declare Revision. Historical sources distinguish significant Version evolution from backward-compatible Revision changes: DF-FND-002 §6.6 and DF-FND-004 §§4.10/6.8. Neither establishes a complete numerical successor contract for this review. The following working rule formalizes that gap while preserving input evidence.

### 5.2. Edition successors

Version uses the observed major.minor numeric form. Revision is a monotonic integer per document across version changes during this review.

| Change | Version action | Revision action |
|---|---|---|
| Compatible correction/clarification/reclassification preserving contractual meaning | Keep Version. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Compatible additive contract capability | Increment minor by one. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Incompatible contract/convention change | Increment major by one and set minor to 0. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Validation/reporting with no source content change | Keep Version. | Keep Revision; track the event centrally. |
| New normalized review document | Initial Version 1.0. | Initial Revision 1; no invented Revision 0 history. |

Explain compatibility per UPDATE. Changing a classification label does not automatically change Version; replacing what a classification/schema contract permits may be incompatible even if no IDs change. Assess changes to identity syntax/resolution separately from a filename correction. Do not reset an existing Revision counter on Version changes during this review. Future alternative numbering requires a traceable policy change, not an implied reset.

Each completed persisted working edition with changed content receives its successor. Draft editing before an edition is finalized is preparation, not evidence of completed intermediate editions. If a validated/finalized edition needs a correction, create another successor and retain the failed validation event. No source revision is incremented merely to record this policy's adoption.

### 5.3. Working lifecycle and Baseline

Edited working documents start at Status=Draft, including successors of received Approved/Canonical documents. A subsequent explicit submission may use Review; formal approval/publication requires its own decision/evidence. Leave untouched source statuses unchanged. Canonical in a received header is preserved as historical evidence, not automatically granted to a successor or silently converted into Approved.

A newly created or modified working edition has Baseline=Not assigned unless its exact inclusion is evidenced. Record original Status and Baseline in the edition history and input manifest. Do not change the original Baseline snapshot. Draft is a lifecycle state; Not assigned is an explicit absence marker in the human-readable working header, not a new Baseline identifier.

At Step 3 creation, this policy and DF-RVW-002 were Draft, Version 1.0, Revision 1, Baseline Not assigned. Current working coordinates follow their headers and exact edition histories. Passing their scoped checks does not approve/publish them or place them in a Baseline. The conventions for these working headers do not populate the canonical Metadata Dictionary or create a Metadata Profile lifecycle event by implication.

## 6. REVIEW, UPDATE, VALIDATE and evidence

Keep Step 1–7 and document substep numbers 4.01–4.87 stable. Step 3.1 identifies this policy; Step 3.2 identifies the consolidated report. The eight functional files keep their scheduled content/reference substeps but have no normalization requirement.

REVIEW reports findings, sections, severity, proposed correction and closure evidence without modifying the reviewed source. UPDATE shows exact material before/after, compatibility assessment, full updated source, diff, edition history, central CHANGELOG entry and Milestone. Mark source corrections pending validation. VALIDATE compares the exact updated edition with its input and affected sources, checks related occurrences and records outcome/limits with SHA-256 evidence. A failure creates a traceable corrective step.

Before any cross-document normative change or path/ID migration, identify the batch, rationale, affected documents and previous/new mapping. Do not claim integrated consistency during partial rollout. Resolve semantic references and actual dependencies separately; do not use a renamed relationship type to conceal a mandatory dependency cycle.

Finding states used for this review are Open, Corrected—pending validation, Closed—verified and Not applicable—scope decision. These tracking states are not document Status, element lifecycle or Milestone Status. Closure requires evidence; scope exclusion requires the specific decision. INV-02 is Not applicable because the user excluded the eight functional files, not because IDs were assigned or validation passed.

The input/final/validated manifests record paths, identity and edition where applicable, SHA-256 and scope. Evidence exports are attached to DF-RVW-002. A manifest's own hash belongs in its delivery receipt/enclosing package, not recursively inside its own contents. A document's hash is recorded outside the document itself. Validation logs do not force recursive revisions of themselves.

## 7. Central CHANGELOG and Milestones

Reuse CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md, retaining their historical content. They remain non-normalized. Keep the CHANGELOG's sequential #, reverse chronology, Author, Type, Document, Impact and Description columns. Add Reviewed and Validated event types to distinguish executed reviews/checks from document content updates; these event Types are not document Type values. Existing Created/Updated/etc. and impact values remain in force.

### 7.1. Cumulative documentary authorship

The normalized document header's **Author** field lists all evidenced authors who contributed to the document, including its original author and contributors to later editions. Use **semicolon followed by a space (`; `)** between distinct authors. Preserve established names and role qualifications; retain first evidenced contribution order and do not duplicate an author for each revision. Example: `Arnaldo Figueira; Codex — AI assistant`.

Carry forward evidenced original/prior authors when preparing a successor. Record each later contributor when that contribution is supported by source history, exact edition/diff evidence or explicit reliable attribution. Preserve edition history separately so the cumulative header does not imply that every listed author performed every change. When original authorship is absent or unknown, list only known contributors and retain that limitation; do not guess an author from ownership, filename, user identity or authorization. A later substantiated attribution receives a traceable correction.

A user who actually edits document content is recorded as an author when that contribution and identity are established. Permission, instructions, approval or file custody alone do not prove an authored contribution. Later disk changes must be examined as resulting bytes with attribution evidence; earlier validation results do not automatically apply. The author list is provenance, not a blanket assignment of approval or responsibility for consequences of every later final product.

### 7.2. Event-specific CHANGELOG authorship

The CHANGELOG **Author** column records the evidenced contributors who performed that particular event, using the same `; ` separator when the event has multiple authors. It is not copied automatically from the cumulative document header. Use `Codex — AI assistant` for events performed solely by this assistant; do not attribute the event to the user merely because the user authorized it. Preserve historical event authors rather than retroactively adding every document author to each row.

For each update, record source path/ID, old/new edition, material change, finding, validation state, report/diff link and Milestone in the Description. Append a later validation event rather than rewriting a pending-validation update into a historical success. Do not log future intentions as completed changes.

### 7.3. Milestone scope and history

Preserve M0–M7. Create M8–M14 for the review's verifiable results, with the existing Not Started/In Progress/Completed milestone states and O/S/C record states. A milestone's state derives from its own records for its declared work scope. Completion of a historical implementation milestone is not closure of a new review milestone.

M8 establishes the received corpus, including explicit limitations. M9 establishes this review's policy, artifact identities, central tracking and scoped checks. M10 covers Foundation cycles; M11 Architecture cycles; M12 the four input Documentation components; M13 localized identity/path/reference reconciliation; M14 integrated validation and final delivery. M9 excludes propagation into all domain sources, which is assigned to M10–M13.

No estimated completion date is invented. Completion dates are actual dates when criteria are satisfied. No new Blocked/Not applicable milestone state is introduced; describe blockers or non-applicable migration scope in the relevant milestone's evidence. A review Milestone=Completed means its documentary criteria were met, not approval, publication, release or Baseline membership.
